text:
andrew: Heads-up thread on API shape for console -> control-plane. We keep oscillating between REST+JSON at the edge vs gRPC proto internal-only. Need a concrete proposal that covers routing headers, quota enforcement points, telemetry invariants, and a safe rollout plan. Thoughts?

raj: my take: use protobufs as source-of-truth for data contracts, but don't force the console to speak gRPC directly. gateway does proto <-> JSON transcode. That lets us keep strong typing server-side while keeping browser ergonomics.

sophie: +1. followup: gateway must be tiny and deterministic. no business logic in it. auth, transcode, header passthrough, and route resolution only. If we start branching logic in gateway we'll create divergence. :warning:

lisa: question: where do routing policies live? in a central policy store (control-plane) or as annotated config attached to routes in the gateway?

maria: prefer central policy store (versioned). gateway pulls policy and caches it. runtime still needs to know selected variant (for telemetry & quotas) so gateway must attach final model_id header. keep human-friendly route names internal to control-plane.

andrew: header list proposal (minimal): X-RW-Tenant, X-RW-Route, X-RW-Model, X-RW-API-Version, X-RW-Trace. Keep names short to reduce overhead.

raj: add X-RW-Client-Build. console teams use it for feature flags and to help triage transport-specific bugs.

sophie: telemetry: every request gets a request_id and emits two events: gateway-observed and runtime-accounting. gateway-observed includes transport, transcode_time_ms, and headers. runtime-accounting includes tokens_consumed, model_id, model_latency_ms, and account_dimensions. correlate by request_id.

lisa: quota enforcement: soft enforcer at gateway (fast rejects), authoritative enforcer in runtime post-accounting. if runtime rejects due to quota, runtime returns specific header X-RW-Quota-Status: throttled and X-RW-Quota-Remaining: 0. gateway should map that to 429 to the client.

maria: also add proactive quota hints in gateway responses when client is near limit: X-RW-Quota-Remaining and X-RW-Quota-Reset so UI can show live meters.

andrew: rollout plan idea: 1) Keep current REST endpoints. 2) Add proto-based gRPC endpoints on same logical path but only accessible via an API-Version header. 3) Run both for 2 weeks while canaries and synthetic checks run. 4) Flip default after monitoring green.

raj: we should auto-instrument transcode latency so we can answer: "how much overhead does transcoding add for p50/p95?" store per-route histograms tagged by transport and canary flag.

sophie: for client SDKs: generate TS types from proto, but ship a tiny runtime that does grpc-web if available and falls back to fetch+JSON. keep the surface stable so console devs import one package.

lisa: security note: if we put route hints in headers, ensure tenant scoping happens before route-to-model mapping. a malicious tenant shouldn't be able to spoof headers to access another tenant's models. gateway must validate Authorization -> tenant mapping and drop/override route headers if mismatch.

maria: agree. also log header mismatches as infra warnings (low severity) to detect accidental leaks.

andrew: sample gateway mock for transcode mapping (for infra docs):

```
# mapping.yaml
- route: "/v1/generate"
  methods:
    - name: Generate
      proto: redwood.inference.v1.Inference.Generate
      json_path: "/v1/generate"
      allowed_clients: ["console", "batch"]
      inject_headers: ["X-RW-Model", "X-RW-Route"]
```

raj: action items: raj -> write client wrapper RFC (proto->ts + fallback) by EOD Friday; lisa -> gateway prototype that preserves headers and emits gateway-observed metric this week; sophie -> telemetry event schema + sample dashboards (latency by transport, transcode overhead) by Wednesday; maria -> policy-store doc + cache invalidation plan by next Tue. andrew -> consolidate rollout + security checks into a short playbook.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: api/transport-canary (starts in 1h) :rocket:

andrew: great. if anyone has objections to proto-as-canonical, speak now otherwise i'll push the migration RFC draft.

sophie: no objections from me. Proto canonical, JSON surface for browser, gateway transcode, two-layer quota model, and telemetry correlation via request_id.

lisa: fine by me. will start the gateway prototype and post a link to the PR.

maria: LGTM. will coordinate with security to add header validation tests.

andrew: thanks all. we'll reconvene after initial metrics from the canary.
